issues.description: Phase 2 is not creating a new useful optimization regime. It only weakens physics weights while keeping the same theory-plus-residual decomposition, so the model remains anchored to the Phase 1 solution.
issues.recommendation: Treat Phase 2 as residual/data adaptation, not just lower-weight physics training. Change gradient routing so the residual and battery/SOC path can improve net MSE without corrupting exogenous physics components.

issues.description: The architecture biases the solution toward theory dominance: pred = theory + residual, while theory_mse and res_reg both discourage the residual from carrying systematic correction.
issues.recommendation: In Phase 2, reduce or remove residual regularization and prevent final net-MSE gradients from rewriting load/PV/wind theory components.

issues.description: The same shared representation is being optimized for net MSE, theory MSE, component MAE, SOC bounds, and residual regularization. In Phase 2, these objectives still conflict even at lower weights.
issues.recommendation: Use selective detach or partial freezing to separate physical component preservation from residual correction.

issues.description: The brief restart improvement to 0.4038 indicates the model can find a better local point, but the current objective or scheduler dynamics pull it back toward the Phase 1 compromise.
issues.recommendation: Reset the Phase 2 optimizer/scheduler state and use a short warmup, but only as a secondary fix after addressing the gradient-routing issue.

issues.description: Longer strong-physics training is likely counterproductive because Phase 1 already reaches its best validation MSE at epoch 8. Additional Phase 1 training can further suppress residual learning.
issues.recommendation: Switch from the best Phase 1 checkpoint, not the last Phase 1 checkpoint, and avoid extending Phase 1 unless component quality is still clearly improving.

recommendations.approach: Selective detach in Phase 2: detach load, PV, and wind, but keep battery/SOC differentiable
recommendations.rationale: Load, PV, and wind are exogenous physical components that should not be rewritten by net-MSE gradients during residual fine-tuning. Battery/SOC is endogenous and should keep gradient flow because it can absorb physically meaningful temporal correction.
recommendations.expected_impact: Most likely to make Phase 2 stable and capable of improving beyond the Phase 1 best.

recommendations.approach: Reset Phase 2 LR schedule and optimizer moments, with a short warmup and lower peak LR
recommendations.rationale: This fixes transition shock from Phase 1 optimizer state. It explains oscillation control, but not the core failure.
recommendations.expected_impact: Helpful when combined with selective detach; unlikely to solve the problem alone.

recommendations.approach: Make Phase 2 explicitly residual-focused: greatly reduce or zero res_reg, keep SOC bounds, keep theory/component losses as weak stabilizers
recommendations.rationale: If residual correction is penalized, Phase 2 cannot learn the systematic error left by the physics prior.
recommendations.expected_impact: Moderate to high, especially if the theory branch has irreducible bias.

recommendations.approach: Do not abandon two-phase training; fix the transition semantics
recommendations.rationale: Phase 1 is clearly useful because it reaches good validation MSE. The failure is that Phase 2 is not structurally different enough from Phase 1.
recommendations.expected_impact: Preserves the benefit of physics pretraining while enabling data-driven correction.

recommendations.rationale: This may reduce curriculum discontinuity, but it does not fix the theory-plus-residual gradient conflict by itself.
recommendations.expected_impact: Possible fallback, not the first fix.

recommendations.rationale: Longer Phase 1 likely strengthens the same physics-dominant basin that blocks Phase 2. Earlier restart may reproduce transient gains but will not make them stable.
